key_insight: λ-MACE enables experimentally accurate hydration free energies, but combining hydration and sublimation calculations still leaves crystalline solubility errors of 1.53 log units.
engineering_relevance: The workflow offers a physics-based route to predict neutral drug solubility from known crystal structures, supporting drug discovery and formulation decisions.
method: Introduce λ-MACE, a machine learning interatomic potential optimized for condensed-phase free energy calculations.
Compute hydration free energies using free energy perturbation.
Combine hydration and sublimation free energies to predict crystalline solubility.
evidence_signal: Evaluation covered 70 medicinally relevant FreeSolv compounds for hydration and 10 additional compounds for solubility, with sublimation accuracy competitive with industry-standard DFT.
watch_item: Solubility error remains above experimental uncertainty of 0.17–0.6 log units; closing the gap requires roughly 0.5 kcal/mol accuracy in each leg, with crystalline thermodynamics the hardest challenge.
paper_title: Computing hydration free energies and crystalline solubility of drug-like molecules with MACE
